correctness.rationale: PASS: On each arm, the Poisson solution is the quadratic torsion profile plus the center-value affine term; the center value is fixed by the Kirchhoff flux condition. Positivity of the inverse identifies its L∞→L∞ operator norm with the maximum torsion function. The slope substitution reduces the arm lengths to a positive quadratic simplex with a fixed sum. Convexity bounds the sum of edge norms by the vertex configurations and yields the strict upper inequality; the Minkowski estimate gives the strict lower inequality. The stated collapsing/equalizing families approach the two constants, while positivity of every arm excludes attainment. Continuity of the maximum on the connected positive-length simplex gives the full open interval. The finite-element/shooting checker is only a consistency test, not the continuum proof.

value.rationale: PASS: The L∞ norm is a natural worst-case Poisson-stability invariant for a star network with fixed total edge length. The exact range and nonattainment identify a counterintuitive design boundary: symmetric arms are not minimax-optimal, and a collapsing absorbing arm lowers the norm. This is a complete geometric classification with meaningful limiting configurations, not a finite numerical census. Its value is the global optimization beyond the known pointwise torsion profile.
